title: Checkpoint 8: Building Protocol
hints: A protocol lists requirements; an extension can implement a requirement for everyone.
Add a `kind` requirement and implement `salesSummary()` once in `extension Building`.
jsBridge: A protocol with a default `salesSummary()` in an extension. This is protocol-oriented programming, sharing behaviour across `House` and `Office` structs without a base class. TS would use an abstract class or a mixin.

compass.q: TS abstract class vs Swift protocol extension: which lets `House` also conform to other protocols freely?
Put `salesSummary` in the extension vs as a requirement: how does that change dispatch (recall the dispatch trap)?
How do you get the type name (`House`) generically: `String(describing: Self.self)`?
Protocol-oriented design is a Swift talking point (WWDC 2015). Where does it go too far?
